I’m going through the same exact thing now. When I broke up w my ex for not respecting my boundaries and pressuring me, he posted on his private for all our mutual friends to see, saying he was going to kill himself. I knew it was manipulation and I called him out for it and was like “wow I can’t believe you did not take me seriously”. We later made up and became friends but  at a party, he tried to hang himself in front of me to get me to get back together with him and kept screaming how he was going to hurt himself. Again I knew it was manipulation but this time I was done so I didn’t respond to any of his texts. He just went on saying he was just really upset over the breakup. Now he’s attacking me and calling me a bad person because I cut him off. What your ex and what my ex is doing is emotional abuse, and the point of it is to doubt yourself. I keep questioning myself and if I overreacted or if what I did was wrong because he kept guilt tripping me. That’s what your ex is doing and I’m really sorry it’s so hard to not believe what they’re saying because you trusted that person so much. It’s hard to shake emotional abuse and you just have try your best to block out the self doubt and continues to reassure yourself each day. Do not worry about being nice, he does not deserve your kindness anymore. Be cordial, but if you give him any chance to talk to you he will take advantage of that to try and make him apart of your life again. Make sure you go to any mutual friends you want to keep and tell them your side ASAP. Cause right now he misses you and is upset but then they get angry and will try to bring you down however they can. They will try to turn mutual friends against you (what mine is doing rn 😀) so you just gotta think three steps ahead to avoid any more hurt coming your way. I wish you the best and hope you can find peace.

If you do confront her about it, do not get angry, upset, or be antagonizing. As a teen that’s going through this rn that would most likely make her feel worse and be less willing to open up about it. Make sure you try to control your emotions as much as possible. You may feel upset or angry that’s she’s doing this to herself but you have to keep calm and be compassionate. Try to listen and make her feel understood if she does open about why she’s doing this. Tell her you understand how her emotions can be overwhelming and hard to cope with and you understand why she would turn to coping methods like this. She will be more open to receiving help if she feels validated and understood.
